title: Legends crowd requests and repertoire
summary: Tunes requested at Legends, tempos, set arrangements and a thousand-tune book.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Here we go. We're on reel three of Luke's Giro. And we were talking about legends and the different tunes and things there. What are the people like there mostly? What kind of tunes they

would ask you for? Well, if they ask for some of the new ones and some of the old ones, some Latin American. It all depends on the crowd. Then you might get an Italian ship in there with some seamen and they'll ask for all the Italian numbers. And all we know is a few of them, like Omarie and Osolamé and a few others. So we tried to please them. And then we had a few numbers like trees and Martha and all, which are a fine number. We sort of played those too. That's our numbers and sometimes they ask for them too. And sometimes they ask for some of the real old ones like Mary Lou, Angry, Tin Roof Blues, High Society or March
of the Bobcats. I know she plays a solo song in March of the Bobcats.

Yeah. See, sometimes I poop out on it. I mean, it has to be a certain, you know, tempo for me. But it's not just right. I mean, it has to be right there. The rhythm and all has to be just right, you know. And I can really hit at it. How fast do you like to play?
Well, what's the fastest you ever like to play on? Well, it all depends on the tune.

Oh, see, sometimes like after you're going like the real things, you know. And, I mean, we can look at the old, it's something like a show tune, in other words, I like to. Or, and, let's see, we have a little arrangement there with four numbers that we play. And I think, you see, the, we see the, we see the first number is, let's see, the Lady of Spain. And then we end up with, you know, Carol Ann in the end. And it's real nice. And in between there's a couple of other tunes. I can't remember the names of them. You play that fast? I mean, it's about, it is real fast, but I mean, it's fast enough that, I mean, you'd have
to really, yeah. Well, stomp off how fast you play after you've gone. Give me the beat, this gentleman. That fast? Uh-huh. You get going on a number like that. Oh, yeah. And then we, you know,

sort of play with a lot of numbers. We have about, oh, about a thousand tunes up there. And, some of them may hardly ever get to play. I mean, sometimes if it's slow that night, we'll sort of go through the books then, you know, sort of make a few medallers. And, boy, it's really, I mean, it's really nice. It's, you know, sort of, you know, brace the monotony.
Some nights do you play nearly all requests? Yeah.

Don't get a chance to do it, yeah. No. Sometimes there's a lot of, there's repeats on numbers, like Release Me and, you know, if you're the, you know, terms like Born Free and Born to Lose and you're cheating hard. But that Release Me, boy, that's been, we didn't really ask for that number.
